doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

chapter: Songs, singers and the state of jazz
title: Newer jazz singers she likes
summary: She names Vanessa Rubin, Lorez Alexandria, her sister-in-law Della Griffin and others.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: That we won’t talk about. Those kind of places. Are there people out, new jazz singers, that you enjoy these days? Do you get a chance to listen much?
I don’t hear too much but I like Vanessa, Vanessa Rubin. Are you familiar with her?
And I still like Lorez Alexandria. Are you familiar with—?
But she’s not a new singer. Della Griffin. Have you heard of her?

That’s my sister-in-law. She’s just new recording, and she’s been singing a long time, but they’re just beginning to hear her, but she’s a very wonderful singer. So I like her. And there’s a young lady, her name is Denia, Denia Green. But I don’t know if she’s recorded yet or not, but she’s very good. I know you’re speaking of probably you’re speaking of Dianne Reeves, and I’m not too familiar with them, Dianne Reeves, and Krall?
I’m not familiar with them, and some other singer they asked me did I hear — I can’t think of her name.
